v.why: A direct 3x3 route to the output already supplies capacity, so the final-edge conv is more substitutable.
Parallel conv routes into node 3 partly substitute, so the second conv adds less.
Without a direct route the output depends on the deeper paths, so improving edge 5 matters more.
With no direct edge, edge 4 is a main route to the output, so a conv there has more leverage.
When node 2 holds conv-processed features, an identity from node 2 to the output forwards them cleanly.
A 3x3 on edge 0 already supplies spatial context and depth, so a second serial 3x3 adds diminishing returns.
Replacing a direct 3x3 conv with identity discards learned capacity, so the edit is worse than on average.
Replacing a useful identity shortcut with a conv gives little gain, unlike replacing weak ops such as pool or none.
The existing identity on the final edge is already a good op, so swapping it for a conv gains less than replacing a weak op.
A direct identity route to the output eases optimization and is a large gain over having no direct edge.
